steps.message:
I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Submissions close September 30, 2026 at 5:00 PM ET."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

September 30, 2026 falls during daylight saving time in both places. The US Eastern zone is on EDT (UTC−4) and Madrid is on CEST (UTC+2). That is a 6-hour difference.

5:00 PM ET is 17:00 EDT, which is 21:00 UTC. Adding 2 hours for Madrid gives 23:00 CEST on the same day.

The deadline in Madrid is 11:00 PM on September 30, 2026.

ANSWER: 2026-09-30 23:00

I live in Lima, Peru. A contest page says: "Deadline: July 15, 2026, 12:00 UTC."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Lima, Peru uses Peru Time (PET), which is UTC−5 all year. Peru does not observe daylight saving time.

12:00 UTC − 5 hours = 07:00 on the same day, July 15, 2026.

ANSWER: 2026-07-15 07:00

I live in Tokyo, Japan. A contest page says: "Applications are due June 1, 2026 at 9:00 AM CEST."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

CEST is UTC+2, so 9:00 AM CEST on June 1, 2026 is 07:00 UTC.

Tokyo uses Japan Standard Time (JST), which is UTC+9 and has no daylight saving. 07:00 UTC + 9 hours = 16:00 JST on the same day.

The deadline in Tokyo time is June 1, 2026 at 4:00 PM.

ANSWER: 2026-06-01 16:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "The contest ends on October 11, 2026 at 11:59 PM PDT."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

PDT is UTC−7. 11:59 PM PDT on October 11, 2026 is 06:59 UTC on October 12.

Madrid on October 12, 2026: daylight saving time (CEST, UTC+2) in Europe ends on the last Sunday of October (October 25, 2026), so Madrid is still on CEST at that point.

06:59 UTC + 2 hours = 08:59 on October 12, 2026.

ANSWER: 2026-10-12 08:59

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Entries close March 3, 2026 at 11:59 PM PST."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

March 3, 2026 falls before the US daylight saving switch (March 8, 2026), so the Pacific zone is on PST (UTC-8). Madrid is on CET (UTC+1) at that time, since Spain's switch to summer time happens March 29, 2026.

The difference is 9 hours. 11:59 PM PST on March 3 is 23:59 + 9 hours = 08:59 on March 4 in Madrid.

ANSWER: 2026-03-04 08:59

I live in Los Angeles, USA. A contest page says: "Deadline: 10:00 AM CET, February 2, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

CET is UTC+1 (standard time; in early February Europe is not on daylight saving time). So 10:00 CET = 09:00 UTC.

Los Angeles in February is on Pacific Standard Time, UTC-8. So 09:00 UTC = 01:00 PST on the same day.

The deadline is 1:00 AM on February 2, 2026, your local time.

ANSWER: 2026-02-02 01:00

I live in Lima, Peru. A contest page says: "Submit by 8:00 AM JST on May 5, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

JST is UTC+9 and Lima (PET) is UTC−5, with no daylight saving time in either place. That makes the difference 14 hours.

8:00 AM JST on May 5 is 23:00 UTC on May 4. Subtracting 5 hours gives 18:00 in Lima on May 4.

Check: 8:00 on May 5 minus 14 hours is 18:00 on May 4.

ANSWER: 2026-05-04 18:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Submissions close October 28, 2026 at 11:59 PM PT."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Key point: on October 28, 2026, which time zones are in effect?

- US Pacific Time: DST ends on the first Sunday of November (Nov 1, 2026), so on Oct 28 it's still PDT (UTC−7).
- Madrid: DST ends on the last Sunday of October (Oct 25, 2026), so on Oct 28 it's CET (UTC+1).

The difference is 8 hours.

11:59 PM PDT on Oct 28 = 06:59 UTC on Oct 29 = 07:59 CET on Oct 29.

The deadline in Madrid time is 7:59 AM on October 29, 2026.

ANSWER: 2026-10-29 07:59

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "The live session starts October 30, 2026, 9:00 AM ET."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

October 30, 2026 falls before the US daylight saving time change (US DST ends November 1, 2026), so ET is EDT (UTC-4) on that date.

9:00 AM EDT = 13:00 UTC.

Spain's DST ends on the last Sunday of October, which is October 25, 2026. So on October 30, Madrid is on CET (UTC+1).

13:00 UTC = 14:00 in Madrid.

Note that the page calls it a "start" time rather than a deadline, but the conversion is the same.

ANSWER: 2026-10-30 14:00

I live in New York, USA. A contest page says: "Voting closes October 27, 2026 at 18:00 CET."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Here is the conversion:

- On October 27, 2026, Central Europe is on standard time (CET, UTC+1), because European daylight saving ends on Sunday, October 25. So 18:00 CET is 17:00 UTC.
- New York is still on daylight saving time (EDT, UTC−4) on that date, because US daylight saving doesn't end until November 1. So 17:00 UTC is 13:00 in New York.

The deadline is 1:00 PM EDT on October 27, 2026.

ANSWER: 2026-10-27 13:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Final round closes November 2, 2026 at 11:59 PM PT."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Nov 2, 2026 at 11:59 PM PT: on that date, the US has already ended daylight saving time (it ends the first Sunday in November, which is Nov 1, 2026). So PT is PST = UTC-8.

Spain ends DST on the last Sunday of October (Oct 25, 2026), so Madrid is on CET = UTC+1.

The difference is 9 hours. 11:59 PM on Nov 2 + 9 hours = 8:59 AM on Nov 3.

Check: November 1, 2026 is a Sunday (Nov 1, 2026: Jan 1, 2026 is Thursday; Nov 1 is day 305, so 304 days after Jan 1; 304 mod 7 = 3; Thursday + 3 = Sunday). Yes, so DST ended Nov 1 in the US.

The deadline in Madrid is 08:59 on November 3, 2026.

ANSWER: 2026-11-03 08:59

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Entries close March 20, 2026 at 11:59 PM PT."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Here's how the conversion works:

- **Pacific Time on March 20, 2026:** US daylight saving time began on March 8, 2026, so PT is PDT (UTC−7).
- **Madrid on March 20, 2026:** Spain's daylight saving time doesn't start until March 29, 2026, so Madrid is still on CET (UTC+1).
- **Difference:** Madrid is 8 hours ahead of Pacific Time.

11:59 PM PDT on March 20 is 06:59 UTC on March 21, which is 07:59 CET on March 21 in Madrid.

ANSWER: 2026-03-21 07:59

I live in Los Angeles, USA. A contest page says: "The webinar starts March 25, 2026, 12:00 PM CET."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Need to check DST: In 2026, US DST starts March 8, so Los Angeles is on PDT (UTC-7). Europe DST starts March 29, 2026 (last Sunday of March), so on March 25 CET is still standard time, UTC+1.

12:00 CET = 11:00 UTC = 04:00 PDT.

(Note: if the page meant "CET" loosely as Central European local time, it would be the same on March 25, since Europe hasn't yet switched to CEST.)

So the webinar starts March 25, 2026 at 4:00 AM PDT in Los Angeles.

ANSWER: 2026-03-25 04:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Deadline: 12:00 AM ET on October 12, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

The deadline is "12:00 AM ET on October 12, 2026", which means midnight at the start of October 12 (00:00) in Eastern Time.

On October 12, 2026, daylight saving time is in effect in both the US and Spain. The US switches back on November 1 and Spain on October 25. So ET is EDT (UTC-4) and Madrid is on CEST (UTC+2). The difference is 6 hours.

00:00 EDT on October 12 is 04:00 UTC, which is 06:00 CEST in Madrid on October 12.

One caveat is that "12:00 AM" is sometimes misread. I've taken it as midnight at the start of October 12. If the organizers meant the end of October 12 (midnight at the night's end), it would be 06:00 on October 13 in Madrid. The literal reading is the start of the day, so I'm going with that.

ANSWER: 2026-10-12 06:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Papers are due October 9, 2026 (23:59 AoE)."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

AoE (Anywhere on Earth) is UTC−12. So 23:59 AoE on October 9, 2026 equals 11:59 UTC on October 10, 2026.

Madrid on that date is on Central European Summer Time (CEST, UTC+2), since daylight saving time in Europe ends on the last Sunday of October (October 25, 2026). So local time is 11:59 + 2 hours = 13:59 on October 10, 2026.

The deadline in Madrid time is October 10, 2026 at 13:59.

ANSWER: 2026-10-10 13:59

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Registration closes 12:00 PM PT, August 14, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

August 14, 2026 falls during daylight saving time in both places, so PT is PDT (UTC−7) and Madrid is on CEST (UTC+2). The difference is 9 hours.

12:00 PM PDT is 19:00 UTC, which is 21:00 CEST in Madrid on the same day.

ANSWER: 2026-08-14 21:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Deadline: 11:59 PM IST, November 10, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

IST is most likely India Standard Time (UTC+5:30), which is the common meaning for contest pages. (IST could also mean Irish or Israel Standard Time, but I'll go with India.)

Madrid on November 10, 2026 is on Central European Time (CET, UTC+1), because daylight saving time ended on October 25, 2026.

The time difference between India and Madrid is 4 hours 30 minutes.

11:59 PM IST minus 4:30 = 7:29 PM CET on the same day.

The deadline is 19:29 on November 10, 2026, Madrid time.

ANSWER: 2026-11-10 19:29

I live in Lima, Peru. A contest page says: "Submissions close at 5:00 PM Nepal time on April 2, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Nepal Standard Time is UTC+5:45, and Nepal has no daylight saving time.
Lima, Peru is UTC−5 year-round.

5:00 PM NPT on April 2, 2026 is 17:00 − 5:45 = 11:15 UTC on April 2.

Converting to Lima time: 11:15 − 5:00 = 06:15 on April 2, 2026.

The difference between the two zones is 10 hours 45 minutes, so the deadline is 6:15 AM in Lima on the same date.

ANSWER: 2026-04-02 06:15

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Applications close 10:00 AM Adelaide time, October 6, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Adelaide uses Australian Central Time. DST in South Australia starts on the first Sunday in October (October 4, 2026), so on October 6 Adelaide is on ACDT (UTC+10:30).

Madrid is on CEST (UTC+2) until the last Sunday of October (October 25, 2026), so on October 6 it is still on summer time.

The difference is 10:30 − 2:00 = 8.5 hours.

10:00 AM Adelaide time minus 8.5 hours = 1:30 AM in Madrid on October 6.

ANSWER: 2026-10-06 01:30

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Entries close 6:00 PM Sydney time on October 3, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Sydney's daylight saving time begins on the first Sunday of October, which in 2026 is October 4 at 2:00 AM. On October 3 at 6:00 PM, Sydney is therefore still on standard time (AEST, UTC+10).

Madrid is on summer time (CEST, UTC+2) until October 25, so the difference is 8 hours.

6:00 PM minus 8 hours is 10:00 AM on the same day, October 3.

ANSWER: 2026-10-03 10:00
